questions.prompt: Put these five stages of the Procure-to-Pay process, per Lesson 1, in the correct order.
items: A requester identifies a need and submits a requisition (Self Service Procurement)
A buyer converts the approved requisition into a formal purchase order with a supplier (Purchasing)
The goods arrive, or the service is performed, and someone confirms it (Receiving)
The supplier's invoice is matched and validated against the purchase order (Payables)
The company pays the supplier, and the transaction's accounting lands in the General Ledger
questions.explain: Procure-to-Pay always runs through these five stages in order: requisition, purchase order, receipt, invoice, then payment and posting. Each stage is typically owned by a different person and a different work area, which is exactly why following one transaction across all five matters.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a person explicitly granted the ability to act as a buyer within a specific procurement business unit — the role that lets Marcus Ibarra create and manage purchasing documents for LTV's procurement BU — is called a procurement ________.
questions.explain: Being named a procurement agent is what actually grants Marcus the ability to act as a buyer. Without that agent assignment tied to LTV's procurement BU, he could have every job role and privilege in the world and still not be allowed to own a purchase order in that BU.

questions.prompt: LTV Manufacturing's plant is its own requisitioning business unit, but a single corporate procurement BU handles the actual buying for it (and potentially other plants too). What does this arrangement represent?
options: Centralizing the purchasing function into one procurement BU that provides purchasing services to one or more requisitioning BUs
An error in setup, since a requisitioning BU must always also be its own procurement BU
A sign that LTV has not yet assigned the Procurement business function to any BU
A temporary configuration only used during system testing, never in production
questions.explain: A single procurement BU can provide purchasing services to one or many requisitioning BUs, which is common when a company centralizes buying into a shared services function instead of letting every plant or department negotiate separately with suppliers on its own.

questions.prompt: Match each core P2P role to what it actually does, per Lesson 2.
right: Confirms goods arrived or services were performed, using the Receiving work area
Submits a requisition for goods or services through Self Service Procurement
Enters, matches, and validates supplier invoices in the Invoices work area
Processes requisitions into purchase orders and manages the supplier relationship
questions.explain: The requester (Dana) submits the requisition. The buyer (Marcus) processes it into a purchase order and manages the supplier relationship. Receiving personnel (Priya) confirm physical delivery. The AP processor (Chen) enters, matches, and validates the invoice.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about work areas and function security in Oracle Fusion Procurement, per Chapter 1.
options: A work area is the landing page a user opens, scoped to the tasks their role needs, while a module is how Oracle organizes functionality and security behind the scenes
A requester's Self Service Procurement work area shows everything a buyer or AP processor can see, so every role shares the same view
Segregation of duties (SoD) policies can prevent the same person from both creating and approving a purchase order over a certain value
Job roles are built from duty roles, which grant specific privileges like creating a requisition or approving a purchase order
An approver is always a dedicated job role of its own, never a side responsibility layered onto someone's regular job
questions.explain: A work area is the role-scoped landing page built on top of a module. SoD policies can block the same person from both creating and approving above a threshold. Job roles are built from duty roles granting specific privileges. A requester's work area deliberately hides what a buyer or AP processor would need, and an approver role is usually a side responsibility layered onto someone's regular job, not a dedicated one.

questions.prompt: In Oracle Fusion Self Service Procurement, what is a 'non-catalog request'?
options: A request method where the requester manually enters a description, category, estimated price, and supplier because the item isn't available in any catalog
A request made by leaving Oracle Fusion temporarily to shop on a supplier's own catalog website, then returning with a populated cart
A guided form used for a category of request that needs structured information beyond just an item and quantity
A request a buyer creates directly in the Purchase Orders work area, bypassing Self Service Procurement entirely
A request that can only be submitted by a procurement manager, never by an ordinary requester
A request Oracle Fusion generates automatically whenever a catalog item's negotiated price changes
questions.explain: A non-catalog request is used when the item a requester needs isn't in any catalog: the requester manually enters a description, category, estimated price, and supplier, which gives the buyer more to validate later but lets the process continue for one-off or unusual needs.
questions.distractorExplain: Option B describes punchout, not a non-catalog request — punchout sends the requester to a supplier's own website to shop an existing catalog, while a non-catalog request exists specifically because no catalog, supplier site or otherwise, has the item at all. The two are both ways of handling an item without a pre-loaded internal catalog entry, but they work in opposite directions.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: on its own, a requisition has no effect on the supplier and creates no purchase order — it must be approved and then processed into a ________.
questions.explain: A requisition is only a request. It has no effect on the supplier and creates no purchase order by itself; it has to be approved and then processed into a purchase order before the supplier is involved at all.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of Dana's requisition, from creation through handoff to a buyer, in the correct order.
items: Dana opens Self Service Procurement, and her requisitioning BU and deliver-to location default from her employee setup
Dana searches the catalog, adds 50 units of the PB-4400 bearing, and the line's estimated amount calculates automatically
Dana reviews her cart and clicks submit, and the requisition is assigned a requisition number
The requisition routes through Oracle Fusion's BPM-based approval engine to her direct supervisor
Once approved, the requisition lands in Marcus's Process Requisitions worklist to be processed into a purchase order
questions.explain: Header fields default from Dana's own setup first, then the catalog search populates the line and its estimated amount. Submitting assigns a requisition number and sends it into approval. Only after approval does it land in a buyer's worklist to become a purchase order.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about requisition approval rules, per Lesson 7.
options: Approval rules can consider the requested amount, the item category, the business unit, and the requester's position in the supervisory hierarchy
Every requisition, regardless of amount or category, is approved by exactly one hard-coded approver: the requester's direct manager
A rejected requisition returns to the requester with a reason and can be revised and resubmitted, which restarts the applicable approval routing
Increasing a requisition's quantity after partial approval can trigger reapproval if it now crosses a threshold the original routing didn't anticipate
While a requisition is pending, the requester can push it forward out of the approver's queue themselves
questions.explain: Approval rules are configurable and can factor in amount, category, BU, and hierarchy — not a single hard-coded approver. Rejection sends the requisition back for revision and restarts routing on resubmission. A change that crosses a threshold can trigger reapproval. A requester can see where a pending requisition sits but cannot push it forward themselves — that's the approver's action.

questions.prompt: Dana's distribution for the pump bearing defaults to a maintenance expense account on her plant's cost center rather than an inventory or material account. Why?
options: Because Industrial Pump Bearing PB-4400 is categorized as an MRO expense item rather than a stocked inventory asset item
Because expense accounts are always used whenever encumbrance accounting is disabled, regardless of item type
Because Dana, as the requester, manually typed in the maintenance expense account on the requisition line
Because Marcus, the buyer, overrode the default account when he processed the requisition into a purchase order
questions.explain: The charge account defaults based on rules drawing on the requester's own default expense account, the deliver-to location or cost center, and the item category. Because the PB-4400 bearing is categorized as an MRO expense item rather than an inventory asset item, the default resolves to a maintenance expense account instead of an inventory or material account.

questions.prompt: Match each purchasing document type to what it actually is, per Lesson 10.
right: A longer-term legal agreement with a supplier, often covering terms and conditions, without necessarily specifying particular items or prices
Used for a one-time purchase where the item, quantity, estimated cost, and delivery schedule are already known
An individual order issued against an existing blanket purchase agreement as an actual need arises, behaving like its own smaller purchase order
Locks in negotiated prices with a specific supplier over time, without yet knowing the exact delivery schedule or total quantity
questions.explain: A standard purchase order fits a fully defined, one-time need. A blanket purchase agreement locks in pricing over time without a known schedule. A contract purchase agreement covers longer-term legal terms without necessarily naming items or prices. A blanket release is the individual order fulfilled against an existing BPA.

questions.prompt: Dana's bearing purchase becomes a standard purchase order rather than a blanket release, even though LTV already has a pricing relationship with Meridian for this part. Why?
options: Because the specific order for 50 units is a one-time, fully defined need — known item, quantity, price, and delivery date — which is exactly the profile a standard purchase order is built for
Because blanket purchase agreements can only be used for services, never for physical goods like bearings
Because Meridian Bearing Supply Co. does not support blanket purchase agreements as a supplier
Because a blanket release can only be issued if a contract purchase agreement already exists, which LTV has not set up
questions.explain: A standard purchase order is the right choice when a specific, defined need exists right now: known item, quantity, price, and delivery date — exactly Dana's situation. If LTV instead ran high volumes of recurring bearing purchases against a negotiated blanket agreement, Marcus might issue a release against it instead, but this one-time, fully defined order doesn't call for that.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Oracle Fusion tracks a change order as a new, numbered ________ of the same purchase order, rather than as a silent edit — preserving the full history of what changed, by whom, and when.
questions.explain: A change order modifies an already-approved purchase order but is tracked as a new, numbered version of the same document rather than a silent edit, so a consultant or auditor can see exactly what the purchase order looked like before and after each change.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about purchase order statuses, per Lesson 14.
options: Closed for Receiving means no further receiving activity is expected, though invoicing can still occur
Finally Closed means all receiving and invoicing activity has fully completed, and the purchase order is eligible to be archived
Cancelled means the order was fulfilled exactly as intended but is simply being archived ahead of schedule
A purchase order can close automatically when quantities are fully received and invoiced and tolerance settings are met
Cancelling a line that already has a receipt or invoice against it is just as simple as cancelling a line with no activity yet
questions.explain: Closed for Receiving and Finally Closed both describe fulfillment winding down as described. Purchase orders can close automatically once quantities and tolerances are satisfied. Cancelled, by contrast, means the order will not be fulfilled at all — the opposite of 'fulfilled as intended' — and cancelling a line with existing receipt or invoice activity is restricted or requires special handling, not simple.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of the purchase order's lifecycle, from draft through end of life, in the correct order.
items: Marcus processes Dana's approved requisition line into a draft standard purchase order
Marcus submits the purchase order, and it is approved by his procurement manager, reaching status Open
The approved purchase order is communicated to Meridian Bearing Supply Co. through the Supplier Portal
Once the full quantity is received and the invoice is fully matched and paid, the purchase order moves through Closed for Receiving and Closed for Invoicing
The purchase order reaches Finally Closed, with no further activity expected
questions.explain: A draft purchase order is created from the requisition, submitted and approved into Open status, then communicated to the supplier. Only after both receiving and invoicing activity complete does it progress through the Closed statuses and finally reach Finally Closed.

questions.prompt: What is the key structural difference between a receipt and an invoice, per Lesson 15?
options: A receipt confirms physical reality — that goods arrived or a service was performed — while an invoice confirms a financial claim of what the supplier says it is owed
A receipt and an invoice are two names for the exact same document, created at different points in the process
A receipt can only be created after the invoice has already been fully validated
An invoice always has to exist before a receipt can be created
questions.explain: Receiving records that goods arrived or a service was performed — physical reality. An invoice is a financial claim of what the supplier says it's owed. Keeping these as separate documents is exactly what makes three-way matching possible later: the invoice can be checked against both what was ordered and what was actually received.

questions.prompt: Match each receiving concept to what it actually controls, per Lesson 16.
right: A profile option letting a user override the configured routing method at the point of receipt
The shipment is received and put away into its final location in a single transaction, with no inspection
The shipment must be formally inspected, with accept/reject dispositions, before put-away
The shipment is received into a receiving location first, with put-away as a separate later transaction and no formal inspection
questions.explain: Direct delivery skips both a separate put-away step and inspection. Standard receipt separates put-away from receiving without a formal inspection. Inspection required adds a formal accept/reject step before put-away. The Allow Routing Override profile option lets a user override any of these at the point of receipt.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a ________ reverses a receipt, in whole or in part, and sends material back to the supplier — typically because it failed inspection, arrived damaged, or was the wrong item.
questions.explain: A return to supplier reverses a receipt, in whole or part, sending material back because of a physical problem with the goods. Creating one reduces the quantity considered received against the purchase order schedule.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about Receipt Accounting and accruals, per Lesson 18.
options: Inventory (asset) items are always accrued on receipt, with no option to defer it
Period-end accrual is only used for expense items, and only when configured that way
Perpetual accrual waits until period end to create the accrual journal
LTV's bearing, though configured as an expense item, uses on-receipt accrual because its Accrue Expense Items option is set to receipt
The receipt accrual journal credits accounts payable liability directly, the same account the invoice later uses
questions.explain: Inventory items always accrue on receipt with no deferral option, and period-end accrual is only available for expense items when configured that way. LTV's bearing is an expense item but accrues on receipt because of its Accrue Expense Items setting. Perpetual accrual creates the journal the moment of receipt, not at period end — that's period-end accrual's description, not perpetual's. And the receipt journal credits an uninvoiced receipts accrual account, not accounts payable liability directly; the invoice accounting is what later debits that accrual and credits AP.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of the inspection-required routing path, for LTV's bearing receipt, in the correct order.
items: Priya's receipt for the bearings is created and accepted against the purchase order
Because the item is routed for inspection, the quantity moves into an inspection queue
An inspector examines the shipment against the purchase order's specification
The inspector records a disposition — accept, reject, or a split
Accepted material proceeds to put-away into inventory, and Receipt Accounting creates the accrual journal
questions.explain: A receipt is created first, then inspection-required routing moves the quantity into an inspection queue instead of direct put-away. The inspector examines the goods and records a disposition. Only accepted material is put away, and that acceptance is what triggers the receipt accrual journal.

questions.prompt: What does 3-way matching check that 2-way matching does not?
options: That the quantity billed on the invoice is also at or below the quantity actually received, not just at or below the quantity ordered
That the invoice price is at or below the purchase order price
That the purchase order was approved before the invoice was ever created
That the supplier's tax registration is valid
That the requisition was approved by the correct cost center owner
That the invoice was received before the purchase order's need-by date
questions.explain: 2-way matching only checks the invoice against the purchase order: price at or below PO price, quantity billed at or below quantity ordered. 3-way matching adds the receipt, requiring quantity billed to also be at or below quantity actually received — the right control whenever physical delivery matters, exactly LTV's situation.
questions.distractorExplain: Option B describes the price check, but that check already exists under plain 2-way matching — it is not something 3-way matching adds on top. What 3-way matching uniquely adds is comparing the invoice against the receipt, which 2-way matching never looks at at all.

questions.prompt: When Chen's invoice for the bearings is accounted, what happens to the uninvoiced receipts accrual account that Priya's receipt credited back at receiving?
options: The invoice accounting debits that same accrual account, clearing it, and credits accounts payable liability instead
The accrual account is left untouched, and a brand-new, unrelated liability account is created for the invoice
The accrual account is credited a second time, doubling the recorded liability
The accrual account is debited only if the invoice amount happens to differ from the receipt's accrued amount
questions.explain: The invoice accounting debits the same uninvoiced receipts accrual account the receipt credited, clearing it, and credits accounts payable liability — converting a generic 'we owe someone for received goods' accrual into a specific liability to Meridian's named invoice.

questions.prompt: Match each reconciliation or accounting concept to what it actually does, per Lessons 21 and 22.
left: AP trial balance to GL reconciliation
right: Tracing a journal line in the General Ledger backward to the specific subledger transaction that created it
The engine that applies accounting rules to a subledger's events and creates the balanced journals transferred to the General Ledger
Comparing total outstanding, unpaid AP liabilities per Payables against the corresponding liability balance in the General Ledger
Comparing the uninvoiced receipts accrual balance against the corresponding GL accrual account and investigating receipts with no matching invoice
questions.explain: AP trial balance to GL reconciliation compares Payables' outstanding liability total against GL. Accrual reconciliation compares the uninvoiced receipts accrual against GL and chases receipts with no invoice. Drilling down traces a GL journal back to its source. Subledger Accounting is the engine translating subledger events into the journals that reach GL in the first place.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Oracle Fusion Payables does not usually pay invoices one at a time — a ________ selects a batch of eligible invoices and generates payments for all of them together.
questions.explain: A Payment Process Request selects a batch of eligible invoices based on criteria like due date, supplier, business unit, or payment method, and generates payments for all of them together as part of a regular payment run.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about matching holds and tolerances, per Lessons 19 and 23.
options: Tolerances are configured percentages or amounts that allow minor price or quantity variance through without creating a hold
A held invoice can still be paid on schedule — the hold is just a note added to the audit trail
An invoice billing for more units than were ordered and received, outside tolerance, triggers a matching hold
The first question when an invoice 'won't pay' is whether it has a hold, and what kind
Matching holds exist only for price variances, never for quantity variances
questions.explain: Tolerances let minor variance through without a hold. An over-billed quantity outside tolerance triggers a matching hold. Troubleshooting an unpaid invoice starts with checking for a hold and its type. A held invoice cannot actually be paid until the hold is resolved, and matching holds can be triggered by either price or quantity variance, not price alone.

questions.prompt: Put LTV's document chain, per Lesson 24, in the order each document was created.
items: Requisition number — created when Dana submits her request
Purchase order number — created when Marcus processes the approved requisition, referencing it
Receipt number — created when Priya receives the shipment, referencing the purchase order
Invoice number — created when Chen enters Meridian's invoice, referencing both the purchase order and the receipt
Payment — created when a Payment Process Request disburses funds, referencing the invoice
questions.explain: Every document after the requisition points back to the one that created the need for it: requisition, then purchase order, then receipt, then invoice, then payment — the full chain summarized in Lesson 24's walkthrough.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about the three exception scenarios in Lesson 25.
options: A price variance 8% above the PO price, outside tolerance, creates a matching hold until Meridian issues a corrected invoice
When Meridian ships only 45 of 50 bearings, Priya should still receive 50 units to keep the purchase order's numbers consistent
If an invoice for the full 50 units arrives before all 50 have actually been received, it can fail 3-way matching on quantity and go on hold
A return discovered after the invoice has already been paid can typically be unwound by simply reversing the original receipt and invoice
A post-payment return is harder to unwind than a pre-invoice return because cash has already moved and the accounting has likely already posted and closed for the period
questions.explain: The price-variance exception creates a hold until corrected. An invoice for 50 units against only 45 received can fail 3-way matching on quantity. A post-payment return is harder precisely because cash and accounting have already moved. Priya must receive exactly what physically arrived (45), not the originally ordered quantity, and a post-payment return requires a debit memo or credit rather than a simple reversal.

questions.prompt: Why is a return discovered two weeks after the invoice has already been paid harder to unwind than the return-to-supplier process from Lesson 17?
options: Because the return-to-supplier process in Lesson 17 assumed the return happens before invoicing, while a post-payment return requires a debit memo or credit from the supplier instead of simply reversing documents whose cash and accounting have already moved
Because Oracle Fusion technically prevents any return from being processed more than 24 hours after receipt
Because a return-to-supplier can only be used for services, never for physical goods like bearings
Because the purchase order would have to be recreated entirely from a new requisition
questions.explain: Lesson 17's return-to-supplier process assumes the return happens before invoicing. A return discovered after payment is materially different: the cash has already moved and the accounting has likely already posted and closed for the period, so it typically requires a debit memo or credit from the supplier rather than simply reversing the original receipt and invoice.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a return discovered after an invoice has already been paid typically requires a ________ or credit from the supplier, rather than simply reversing the original receipt and invoice.
questions.explain: A post-payment return typically requires a debit memo or credit from the supplier, separately processed in Payables, rather than simply reversing the original receipt and invoice, since the cash has already moved and the accounting has likely already posted and closed.

questions.prompt: Match each journal from LTV's transaction to its accounting entry, per Lessons 8, 18, 20, and 24.
right: Debits accounts payable liability and credits cash once a Payment Process Request disburses funds
Reserves budget against the maintenance cost center before any purchase order exists, reversing once a purchase order is created
Debits the maintenance expense account and credits an uninvoiced receipts accrual account
Debits the uninvoiced receipts accrual account, clearing it, and credits accounts payable liability
questions.explain: The receipt accrual journal debits expense and credits the uninvoiced accrual. The invoice accounting journal clears that accrual and credits accounts payable. The payment journal debits accounts payable and credits cash. If encumbrance accounting is enabled, approving the requisition reserves budget before any purchase order even exists, reversing once the purchase order is created.
